prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: one transparent 16-cel game animation atlas, newly authored artwork.

Create exactly ONE new square animation atlas, ideally 2048 x 2048 pixels, true RGBA with genuinely transparent empty pixels. The canvas contains precisely 4 columns x 4 rows of equal square tiles, with one complete right-facing infantry rifleman per tile. At 2048 resolution each tile is 512 x 512. No visible tile separators or labels.

Reference role: the infantry sheet already viewed in this conversation, adult-infantry-v13.png, is ONLY a style and character reference, not an edit target. Create entirely new cels, do not repaint, copy, collage, rearrange, or reproduce the reference sheet. Match its muted gritty olive-drab military palette, worn cloth, webbing, tactical equipment, dark rifle and boots, and adult proportions. Use realistic digitally painted anatomy with fine natural material shading, NOT chibi, not oversized heads, not chunky low-resolution pixel sprites.

Background: fully transparent alpha, including the large gutters, internal spaces between limbs and rifle, and all surrounding space. No black or white background, no checkerboard painted into the image, no ground patch, floor, contact shadow, cast shadow, scenery, or lighting effects.

Subject continuity: the SAME realistic adult modern infantry rifleman in every cel, same olive-drab helmet, olive-drab uniform and tactical vest, equipment arrangement, rifle dimensions, dark boots, realistic limb lengths, head size, and body scale. Full body and whole rifle always visible. Camera locked to exact orthographic side view, facing RIGHT in all 16 cels; no perspective turn, no view rotation. Fine restrained shading on the body is allowed. The action is a controlled deliberate lowering of body weight from standing to one knee to prone, with coherent joint articulation. No falling or injury.

Invisible layout and registration: tile coordinates below are LOCAL coordinates measured from each tile's upper-left. Every cel uses the same floor at 92% of tile height, y = 471 at a 512-pixel tile. Any foot sole, knee, hand, or elbow that touches the floor must contact exactly this fixed baseline. Do not vertically center each pose. The standing helmet top is about 27% tile height (y = 138), the stable kneeling helmet top about 49% (y = 251), and the final prone helmet top about 74% (y = 379). Thus standing body height is about 65% of tile, kneeling about 43%, prone about 18%. All joints and body parts keep their physical dimensions: obtain decreasing height by bending and extending the same anatomy, NEVER by scaling low poses down. Place the planted front foot consistently around local x = 58% during frames 1-10. Keep head and rifle generally toward the right half, leaving ample room to the left for legs to extend. Keep all nontransparent pixels inside roughly x = 8%-92% of each tile, with a clear bottom margin below the baseline; let generous unused transparent space remain above the lower poses. At no point may a body part or weapon cross a tile edge.

The 16 cels are ONE continuous sequence in ROW-MAJOR order, left to right, top row to bottom row. Each successive action must be visibly authored and progressively lower, not repeated generic kneeling silhouettes. Helmet height descends monotonically (increasing local y) through the sequence; frames 8 and 9 are the sole deliberate equal-height identical hold. Exactly 16 cels, with 15 distinct poses plus the explicitly requested repeated knee pose.

Detailed pose timing; percentages denote approximate helmet-top position within each tile, NOT rendered text:
ROW 1
1. 27%: upright standing, rifle shouldered and aimed horizontally right, both feet grounded, relaxed adult proportions.
2. 29%: knees unlock slightly; pelvis lowers slightly, front boot remains planted, rifle supported.
3. 32%: clearly deeper knee flexion, rear heel begins lifting as weight shifts forward; head visibly lower than cel 2.
4. 36%: controlled shallow lunge, rear knee travels down toward the baseline, front foot stays planted.
ROW 2
5. 40%: lower lunge, front knee bends further, rear knee halfway toward the ground, torso mostly upright.
6. 44%: deeper lowering, rear knee approaches the ground, weight remains controlled and rifle supported.
7. 47%: rear knee just above the ground, near stable one-knee position, torso and head settle lower.
8. 49%: stable one-knee aiming pose: rear knee grounded on the fixed baseline, front sole planted, front knee raised, rifle supported and aimed right.
ROW 3
9. 49%: EXACT SAME stable one-knee pose as cel 8, same scale, position, silhouette, anatomy, rifle, and ground contact. This is the only intentional duplicate.
10. 53%: from that kneel, torso pitches forward and downward, support hand begins reaching DOWN toward ground while firing hand and shoulder support the rifle.
11. 57%: support hand contacts the fixed ground baseline ahead of the knee, torso lowers further, rear leg starts extending backward.
12. 61%: hand bears weight, elbow bends, torso approaches horizontal, trailing leg extends further left; head remains facing right.
ROW 4
13. 65%: near-prone transition, hips descend, legs lengthen backward at unchanged anatomical size, support elbow approaches the fixed baseline.
14. 69%: support elbow reaches the baseline, pelvis settles lower, body almost horizontal, rifle is brought back to a stable rightward aim.
15. 72%: almost fully prone, both legs extended back, chest and elbows settle, head slightly higher than final frame.
16. 74%: final stable full prone rifle-aimed-right pose, legs fully extended left, boots visible, elbows grounded on the same 92% baseline, rifle horizontal and supported, adult anatomy unchanged.

Critical quality: actual gradual standing-to-kneeling-to-prone body-height transition, planted feet without sliding during kneeling descent, identical knee hold at 8/9, consistent body-part dimensions and equipment, coherent shoulders/elbows/wrists gripping rifle, natural knees/ankles, exactly side-on throughout. Broad transparent side margins accommodate full prone length including boots and rifle. This is a clean cutout atlas intended for extraction, so all background and gutter pixels must truly be transparent.

Avoid: additional people within any cel, extra or missing limbs, distorted anatomy, copied knee silhouettes beyond the one specified hold, waving, raised-overhead arms, climbing, jumping, running, hit reactions, blood, casualty poses, falling, muzzle flash, ground patches, shadows outside the character, typography, UI, guides, borders, numbering, grid lines, watermarks. No text whatsoever. Produce only the single atlas.
